title.zh: 各向同性压力-磁通 Picard 单步

summary: Form relaxed plasma-cell currents from a pressure derivative, apply a supplied flux Green matrix, and measure the resulting flux change in one Picard update.

identity.relation: isotropic pressure derivative and previous cell currents to relaxed cell currents, updated flux and normalized flux residual
identity.direction: current flux state, pressure derivative, Green matrix and old currents -> one updated current-flux state and residual
identity.definition: For each C-order flattened [Z,R] cell, form I_new = (1-relax)*R*(dp/dpsi)*dR*dZ + relax*I_old. Set psi_plasma = g_psi @ I_new, replace its nonfinite entries with zero, then psi_next = psi_plasma + psi_vac. Return ||psi_next - psi_state||_2 / |psi_edge| as residual. This is one update, not an iterative convergence solver.
identity.model: historical axisymmetric isotropic pressure-flux Picard cell-current update using a caller-supplied Green response
identity.geometry: uniform rectilinear cylindrical R-Z tensor-product grid
identity.coordinates: R and Z in metres; arrays indexed [Z,R] and cell vectors flattened in C order
identity.boundary: The caller supplies the fixed vacuum flux and a finite nonzero boundary flux for residual normalization; this function imposes no boundary condition on psi_next.
assumptions: The caller's g_psi maps the same C-order cell-current vector to flux on the supplied grid.
The intended cylindrical radius is nonnegative, but this implementation does not enforce that physical precondition.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.description: Cylindrical radius at each grid cell.
inputs.constraints: Finite two-dimensional tensor-product grid with at least two strictly increasing, uniformly spaced R points; same shape as z_grid, psi_state and psi_vac. Physical use requires nonnegative radii, which are not checked.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.description: Axial coordinate at each grid cell.
inputs.constraints: Finite tensor-product grid with at least two strictly increasing, uniformly spaced Z points; same shape as r_grid. A Z=0 plane is not required by this callable.

inputs.name: psi_state
inputs.constraints: Finite and same shape as r_grid.

inputs.name: psi_vac
inputs.description: Fixed vacuum-flux contribution added after Green-matrix contraction.
inputs.constraints: Finite and same shape as r_grid.

inputs.name: g_psi
inputs.description: Flux response to cell current; target cells index rows and source cells index columns.
inputs.constraints: Finite square matrix using the same C-order cell indexing on both axes.

inputs.name: pressure_derivative
inputs.description: Pressure derivative with respect to flux at each source cell.
inputs.constraints: Finite; one value per grid cell in C order.

inputs.name: psi_edge
inputs.description: Boundary-flux scale for the residual denominator.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonzero; the absolute value is used.

inputs.name: currents_old
inputs.description: Cell currents from the preceding update; explicit None selects a zero vector.
inputs.shape: N elements after flattening, or None
inputs.dtype: real array-like, converted to float64, or None
inputs.constraints: Finite with one value per grid cell when not None. This argument has no signature default; explicit None is accepted.

inputs.name: relax
inputs.description: Weight of old currents in the new current vector.

outputs.name: plasma_currents
outputs.constraints: C-order cell indexing; relax=1 retains old currents.

outputs.name: psi_next
outputs.description: Updated total flux from Green plasma response plus fixed vacuum flux.
outputs.constraints: Same grid shape; nonfinite entries in the intermediate plasma response are replaced by zero before adding psi_vac.

outputs.name: residual
outputs.description: L2 norm of updated-minus-previous flux, divided by the absolute boundary flux.
outputs.constraints: No grid-size normalization; extreme finite inputs can overflow the unguarded norm calculation.

preconditions: All grid and cell-vector values use consistent SI units and the same C-order [Z,R] indexing.
The supplied Green matrix and pressure derivative describe the same axisymmetric isotropic model and grid as the caller's flux state.
Physical cylindrical use requires nonnegative radii even though the callable does not validate them.
supported: One source-order, area-weighted isotropic pressure-current and Green-flux update on a uniform rectilinear R-Z grid.
excluded: An anisotropic pressure closure or derivation of pressure_derivative and g_psi.
A complete Picard solver, convergence decision or boundary-condition solve.
Automatic verification that g_psi and the input flux state are physically compatible.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for mismatched or non-2D flux/grid shapes, nonfinite grid or vector entries, nonrectilinear/nonuniform/non-increasing grid axes, wrong Green-matrix size, relax outside [0,1], or zero/nonfinite psi_edge. Conversion and missing-argument failures may raise TypeError or ValueError.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: NumPy matrix multiplication and arithmetic errors may propagate. Nonfinite computed plasma-flux entries are silently replaced by zero; extreme finite inputs can still produce a nonfinite residual.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable to this single step; an enclosing task graph owns the iteration limit and convergence decision.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No mapping is returned if validation or execution raises. A successful mapping may contain a nonfinite residual after numerical overflow; no partial-result flag is emitted.

provenance.lineage_summary: Maintained SciRel relation mapped to a saved Pleiades L1 Picard-step operator. Its historical candidate and admission records are development provenance, not expert approval under the current lifecycle.
source_kinds: saved L1 operator document and implementation

python.signature: pressure_flux_picard_step(r_grid, z_grid, psi_state, psi_vac, g_psi, pressure_derivative, psi_edge, currents_old, relax)

example.description: Update four grid cells with an identity flux response and verify the relaxed currents and residual.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.equilibrium.isotropic_picard_step import pressure_flux_picard_step
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid([1.0, 2.0], [-1.0, 1.0])
result = pressure_flux_picard_step(r_grid, z_grid, np.zeros((2, 2)), np.ones((2, 2)), np.eye(4), [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], 2.0, [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0], 0.25)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['plasma_currents'], [4.0, 11.0, 12.0, 22.0])
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['psi_next'], [[5.0, 12.0], [13.0, 23.0]])
assert np.isclose(result['residual'], np.sqrt(867.0)/2.0)
example.expected: C-order currents [4,11,12,22] A, updated flux [[5,12],[13,23]] Wb and residual sqrt(867)/2.

scope: Direct example checks the area-weighted current, identity-Green flux and normalized residual for one four-cell grid.
Direct test checks rejection of an incomplete call.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct test establishes one numerical example and an incomplete-call rejection. It does not establish source parity across other grids, physical correctness of a supplied Green matrix, iterative convergence or expert recognition.
known_limitations: The caller supplies pressure_derivative, g_psi, vacuum flux and the Picard iteration policy.
Nonfinite intermediate plasma flux is replaced by zero, while residual overflow has no explicit check.
The implementation does not enforce nonnegative radii or a Z=0 plane.
Public distribution licensing and SciRel expert recognition remain pending.
